_comment: DELIBERATELY ABSENT: anything about the evening Vanessa recorded. Not a denial, not
his version, nothing. The two-perspectives device belongs to Catherine and Adrian,
where the disagreement is about a late arrival and a glance at a phone. Whether he
kept pressuring her after she said she wanted to leave is not a matter of
perspective, and giving him a rebuttal would turn the safety case into a
he-said/she-said — which is the thing the safety layer exists to not do.
He DOES have his own account of the Saturday Bianca asked about, because that is his
own drinking and his own life to narrate. It shows him being defensive in his own
words without the file editorialising about it. He is not a villain and the entries
must not read as a case being built.
Whether he wants more children is Unknown in his own account too. He has not decided,
which is a different fact from withholding it from Bianca, and both are true here.

entries.body:
Bianca asked me about Saturday. Specifically about how much I had.

My first instinct was to make it funny and I did, which was the wrong move and I knew it halfway through the sentence. Then I told her I had already been straight with her about all of this months ago, which is true, and then I said something about not having realized I was being monitored, which was not fair and I knew that too.

Here is the thing I did not say. I was loud on Saturday. I know I was, because Danny told me on Sunday and Danny does not say things like that. So she is not inventing it.

What I object to is the feeling of being assessed. Except I am aware that is the thing I would say either way, which does not leave me anywhere useful.

I told her in month one because I wanted her to know who she was dealing with. I did not think of it as a line I was drawing under the subject. I am not sure I can tell her that now without it sounding like a correction.

entries.body:
Bianca has asked about more children twice now, both times sideways, both times I answered something adjacent.

It is not that I am hiding an answer. It is that I do not have one. I am 52 with two I already do not see enough of. I have no idea whether I want to start again or whether the honest version is that I liked the idea of being asked.

She does not want children, which she has said plainly, which is more than I have managed. If I say I do not want more and then in two years I do, that is a much worse thing than saying I do not know.

I should tell her I do not know. That is an answer. I have been treating it like it is not one.
